The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team** represented Missouri State University in the NCAA Division I women’s basketball season. Here's a comprehensive overview of the team, based on official records, statistics, and contemporaneous reporting:

### **Basic Information**
- **Head Coach**: Kellie Harper (in her 4th season at Missouri State)
- **Conference**: Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)
- **Home Arena**: JQH Arena (Springfield, MO)
- **Record**: **23–10 overall**, **15–3 in the MVC** (tied for 1st place in the regular season)
- **MVC Tournament**: **Champions** — won the MVC Tournament for the 3rd time in program history (and first since 2008)
- **NCAA Tournament**: Received an **at-large bid** (#10 seed in the Stanford Regional); lost in the **First Round** to #7 seed Texas A&M, 57–62

---

### **Season Highlights & Key Achievements**
- **MVC Regular Season Co-Champions**: Shared the 2014–15 MVC title with Northern Iowa (both finished 15–3); it was Missouri State’s first outright or shared MVC regular-season title since 2007.
- **MVC Tournament Champions**:  
  - Defeated #8 seed Southern Illinois (71–53) in the quarterfinals  
  - Beat #4 seed Evansville (68–53) in the semifinals  
  - Won the championship game vs. #2 seed Northern Iowa, **66–62**, in a dramatic, tightly contested final (March 14, 2015, at the Family Arena in St. Charles, MO).  
  - This marked their **first MVC Tournament title since 2008**, and secured the program’s **11th NCAA Tournament appearance**.
- **NCAA Tournament Appearance**: Their first since 2009 — ending a six-year drought. It was the program’s 11th overall NCAA bid (dating back to 1992), and the 4th under Kellie Harper.

---

### **Key Players & Statistics**
#### **Star Performers**
- **Nikki Rogers** (Sr., G):  
  - MVC All-Conference First Team  
  - Averaged **14.4 ppg**, **4.1 rpg**, **3.8 apg**, and **1.8 spg**  
  - Shot **42.6% FG**, **37.7% from 3-pt range**, and **79.0% FT**  
  - MVC Tournament MVP (2015) — scored 19 points in the title game, including critical late baskets and 5 assists.
- **Keeli Becton** (Sr., F/C):  
  - MVC All-Conference First Team  
  - Averaged **13.2 ppg**, **8.5 rpg**, **2.2 bpg**, and **1.2 spg**  
  - Led MVC in blocked shots (2.2 bpg) and ranked top-5 nationally in blocks per game  
  - Strong interior presence—shot 52.6% from the field
- **Brittany Phillips** (Jr., G/F):  
  - MVC All-Conference Second Team  
  - Averaged **11.4 ppg**, **5.4 rpg**, **2.7 apg**, **1.7 spg**, 39.8% 3-pt FG  
  - Key perimeter threat and defensive stopper

#### **Other Contributors**
- **Ashley Turek** (So., C) – Provided depth and rebounding off the bench; 5.1 ppg, 4.0 rpg  
- **Alexandra Kapp** (Jr., G) – Reliable reserve; 6.9 ppg, 2.2 apg, 38.5% 3-pt FG  
- **Amanda Brown** (So., G/F) – Defensive specialist; contributed 5.4 ppg and high-energy play

---

### **Team Stats (2014–15)**
- **Scoring**: 65.9 ppg (110th nationally)  
- **Scoring Defense**: 57.2 ppg (35th nationally)  
- **Field Goal %**: 41.1% (132nd)  
- **3-Point %**: 33.2% (80th)  
- **Free Throw %**: 71.6% (167th)  
- **Rebounding**: +3.4 rebound margin (90th)  
- **Assists/Turnovers**: 13.7 apg / 16.1 tpg (1.22 assist/turnover ratio — middle of the pack)  
- **Defensive Strength**: Ranked **#1 in MVC in scoring defense**, blocks (5.5 bpg), and steals (8.5 spg)

---

### **Notable Games & Streaks**
- Won **13 of their last 14 regular-season games**, including a late-season 10-game winning streak (Jan 25–Feb 28), culminating in clinching the MVC title.  
- Defeated nationally ranked teams:  
  - Beat #23/25 Missouri (a non-conference win on Nov 22, 2014 — 71–66 in Columbia), ending Mizzou’s 21-game home win streak in Mizzou Arena  
  - Also defeated #22 Iowa State (Dec 9, 2014 — 71–65)  
- Their MVC Tournament championship win over UNI was especially notable: UNI had beaten MSU twice in regular season, including a 1-point loss in Springfield — the Lady Bears avenged both with a balanced, resilient performance in the final.

---

### **Postseason & Legacy**
- The 2014–15 season marked a **major program resurgence**, fueled by strong senior leadership (Rogers, Becton, Phillips), disciplined defense, and clutch execution in big moments.  
- It was the **first time since 2006–07** that Missouri State won both the MVC regular-season title and tournament in the same year.  
- The team’s success paved the way for continued competitiveness—Harper would go on to lead MSU to five more NCAA Tournament appearances before departing for Tennessee in 2019.  
- Nikki Rogers became the **only Lady Bear to earn MVC Tournament MVP honors twice**, having also won in 2012 (as a freshman on the 2011–12 team).

---

### **Off-Court Recognition**
- The team earned the **MVC Sportsmanship Award** for women’s basketball in 2015.  
- Multiple players were honored for academic achievement:  
  - Rogers and Becton named to the MVC All-Academic Team (3.0+ GPA, 2+ years of varsity experience).  
- The program was praised for community engagement — over 2,500 hours of service logged by the team in the 2014–15 academic year.

---

### **Post-Season Departures & Impact**
- Seniors **Rogers**, **Becton**, and **Phillips** all graduated, leaving substantial leadership and production voids — but the 2015–16 team still reached the NCAA Tournament (20–14), signaling sustained momentum.  
- Coach Kellie Harper was widely viewed as a rising national coach during this era; her leadership of the 2014–15 team was considered a hallmark of her MSU tenure.
